source.title: IPG PHOTONICS ANNOUNCES LEADERSHIP TRANSITION MARLBOROUGH, Mass. – April 30, 2024 - IPG Photonics Corporation (NASDAQ: IPGP) (“IPG” or the “Company”) today announced that its Board of Directors (the “Board”) has appointed Mark Gitin, 57, as the next Chief Executive Officer of the Company and as a member of the Board, effective June 5, 2024. Dr. Gitin’s appointment follows a robust succession planning process, which was conducted with the assistance of a leading independent search firm and considered both internal and external candidates. Following Dr. Gitin’s addition, the Board will expand to 11 members. Dr. Gitin will succeed Dr. Eugene Scherbakov, 76. Dr. Scherbakov is a co-founder of IPG and has spent 30 years with the Company. He will remain a member of the Board and serve as an advisor to the newly appointed CEO. Dr. Gitin currently oversees the Photonics Solutions Division at MKS Instruments, Inc., a business with more than $1 billion in revenue. Dr. Gitin has more than 30 years of experience in the lasers and optics sector and possesses extensive technical and scientific expertise. Prior to joining MKS, he held several executive roles at Coherent. Dr. Gitin has a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from Cornell University, with a focus on ultra-short pulse lasers. “The entire Board has been focused on the next phase of IPG’s evolution, and we are confident that now is the right moment for an orderly transition to build on the strong foundation that has been established to deliver sustainable and profitable long-term growth,” said John Peeler, Non-Executive Chair of the Board. “After thoroughly reviewing a broad range of candidates, we selected Dr. Gitin to lead IPG due to his track record as a strategic industry leader with the ability to identify and execute growth opportunities. bull_case.evidence: Global fiber laser market size 2026: USD 5.1 B; forecast 2036: USD 15.1 B; CAGR 8.8% (2024‑2032)

bear_case.point: IPG’s revenue is overwhelmingly tied to the cyclical materials‑processing capital‑equipment market, which accounts for 86% of FY2025 sales. A downturn in this sector would directly erode top‑line growth.

Net margin remains razor‑thin, with only 0.6% in Q4 2025, and the company has been reporting negative free cash flow despite sizable cash reserves, signaling weak profitability and potential liquidity strain.
Q1 2026 saw an operating loss of $7.7 M versus a $1.8 M profit in Q1 2025, and gross margin fell from 39.4% to 37.5% YoY, indicating ongoing margin erosion and operational inefficiency.
Advanced Solutions revenue declined 9% YoY to $41.5 M, a key product segment that has not compensated for growth elsewhere, reflecting weakness in a core business line.
A potential $15 M tariff delay could dampen revenue and margin outlook, adding uncertainty to the company’s financial performance.
The planned acquisition of Lumibird Medical up to €350 M may strain IPG’s resources, dilute focus on its core laser business, and introduce integration risk without clear synergy evidence.

macro.narrative: The current expansionary manufacturing environment, reflected in a PMI of 55.6 and new orders at 56.7, signals strong demand for high‑performance fiber lasers used in semiconductor, AI, and advanced packaging. The upward‑sloping yield curve and moderate VIX suggest that borrowing costs are modestly higher but still manageable, while the S&P’s bullish stance supports continued capital spending. Together, these macro signals should lift IPG’s order backlog, support pricing power, and improve margins over the next 2‑4 quarters, though input costs may rise slightly.
